subsection.heading: ### The 6/48 gap is answer-slot binding
subsection.location: under the E3 material, immediately after the main findings table and before '### The TX-03 cliff is content absence'
contains: reconstruction method: both arms rebuilt through the runner's own Planner (experiments/ptr-engine/longrun/run_longrun.py:1562) with send_chat replaced by a recorder; checkpoint_prompt applied as the run loop does (run_longrun.py:3555-3567); prompt_sha256 matched 200/200 rows
structural diff: masking T30 158 lines / 1,611 prompt tokens vs spcc 69 lines / 1,465 prompt tokens, layer_tokens L0=80 L1=20 L2=215 L3=21 L4=2
the one difference that matters: the masking arm replays an ANSWER (Tt): line after every turn's tool-output block; the spcc journal replays no answers at all

quoted masking T31 lines 152-158 (QUESTION (T31): What is VAL_C of doc-fact-08? / TOOL OUTPUTS: / TOOL_OUTPUT (doc-fact-07@1): # doc-fact-07 / VAL_A = 4071 / VAL_B = 4072 / VAL_C = 4073 / VAL_D = 4074) answered 4073 while the expected 4083 sits at line 62 inside TOOL_OUTPUT (doc-fact-08@1) delivered at T11, 90 lines and 428 tokens above the question and the only occurrence of that value
delivery table: 5 turns, delivered document differs from asked document in 5/5, masking answers with the delivered body's value on 4/5, spcc 0/5

refutations: proximity (at T30 masking 32 tokens before / 27 after, spcc 21 before / 17 after, and spcc answers correctly) and document anchoring (the masking arm prints TOOL_OUTPUT (doc-fact-07@1): # doc-fact-07 and the model ignores it)
T12 answer replay: masking T12 line 55 reads ANSWER (T10): ANSWER: NUM 4061 — T10's wrong answer is T12's correct answer, so the value appears twice
within-document failures: T34 answered 4022 = ANSWER (T22): ANSWER: NUM 4022 (same document, different symbol); T73 answered 4124, the line immediately below VAL_C = 4123 in the same body
verdict: intrinsic to a transcript replay that replays answers — the answer replay is load-bearing, so deleting the ANSWER lines turns the arm into the spcc journal
consequence: the 6/48 gap is a format artefact and must be excluded from any retention comparison

next_unit_hint: The 6/48 gap is now recorded and excluded from retention comparisons. Two follow-ups remain separable and both are offline. (1) The answer-slot binding predicts that the masking arm's cross-document errors occur exactly on turns where the fixture delivers a body for a document other than the one asked — 5 such turns exist in TX-04 and 4 fail; a fixture with more delivery/ask mismatches would test that prediction directly with no requests. (2) The d64 result is still a single rep at a noise floor of ±4.2 pp; a second rep at d64 only (9 probes × 2 arms = 18 requests) would put the 9/9 on firmer ground. Do not re-run the full 200-request cell for either.
